name: Herbert Hoover
role: 31st US president (1929–1933); Secretary of Commerce (1921–1928); relief administrator
summary: Republican president and former engineer who described his outlook as American individualism: equality of opportunity, voluntary cooperation, regulation to prevent domination, and a refusal to put government into commercial business. He backed protective tariffs and immigration limits, signed the Smoot-Hawley tariff and founded the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, and after 1933 attacked the New Deal as regimentation.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argued that government is practically incompetent at running commercial business, citing the post-war railways, and that business progress depends on competition.

public-ownership.rationale: Vetoed the Muscle Shoals bill for permanent government power operation, called nationalization of industry the negation of American individualism, and opposed state operation of utilities and railways.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proposed the 1932 tax plan that raised the top income rate to 63 percent and doubled the top estate tax rate, and wrote that some fortunes exceed what incentive requires, but this was a deficit measure and he also urged cutting capital-gains tax.

unions-good.rationale: Listed labor unions among organizations that offer training in responsibility and also warned of arrogant domination by some labor leaders; mixed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wrote that private property is not a fetish in America, citing the uncompensated end of the liquor trade, and treated property as an instrument for initiative rather than an end.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Called for rigid enforcement and extension of federal regulation of utilities and competition law where states cannot act, while also wanting some regulation relaxed.

strong-leader.rationale: In The Challenge to Liberty attacked the vast centralization of power in the Executive under the New Deal.

state-harmful.rationale: Described government as an umpire and encourager of voluntary cooperation, supported public regulation, education and health services, and rejected the idea that the state is harmful in itself.

decide-locally.rationale: Said the American system rests on decentralized local responsibility, limited federal regulation to cases where states lack power, and treated education as primarily a state and local matter.

gradual-change.rationale: Said America kept liberalism alive by reform not revolution and that its system evolves by orderly shifts.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Restricted immigration by administrative order in 1930, called for revision of laws on a more limited and selective basis, and later asked to put restriction into statute and strengthen deportation.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Supported US adherence to the World Court and disarmament conferences but ruled out League of Nations membership or commitments in advance; mixed.

free-trade.rationale: Backed protective tariffs and signed the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act, over objections from economists.

nation-first.rationale: Said US progress is interlocked with the world's and favored international arms limits and the World Court, yet rejected League commitments and later opposed entering the war.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred: favored restricting and selecting immigration and cut it in 1930.

revolution-justified.rationale: Described revolution as a tornado leaving destruction and condemned the hate and murder dressed up as political idealism; stressed reform instead.

experts-over-public.rationale: Wrote that popular desires are no criteria of real need, which must be determined by deliberation, education and leadership, and that the crowd feels but does not plan.

central-planning.rationale: Rejected government direction of production and distribution and called nationalization the negation of American individualism.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Proposed the 1932 tax plan that doubled the top estate tax rate, and held that the sons of the successful should not inherit places of power by birth; he did not argue for it generally.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Signed the Tariff Act of 1930 to protect farmers and industries from foreign competition and defended the protective policy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Said government must keep out of production and distribution of goods and services; its emergency credit lending was temporary.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred: held that self-interest must remain a motive for production for generations and called socialism a failure.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Praised credit expansion by the Federal Reserve System as of incalculable value and urged coordination with central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Opposed the New Deal's regimentation, including the National Industrial Recovery Act, as a form of state dictation of industry.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Treated autocracy by birth or divine right as the opposite of American individualism.

natural-rulers.rationale: Wrote that people differ in ability and that a small percentage of creative minds drives progress, while insisting leadership must rise through competition rather than birth.

war-builds-character.rationale: Described war as destruction that leaves nations poorer and spiritually dislocated.

military-superiority.rationale: Pursued naval limitation and parity with other powers and sought to cut arms rather than outbuild rivals.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Inferred: rejected class frameworks and Marxist doctrine in favor of equality of opportunity.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Wrote that Americans do not pretend that all people are equal in ability and that government can assure only liberty, justice and equality of opportunity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Called self-interest a necessary motive for production but said civilization cannot rest on unrestrained self-interest.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Celebrated the gains in living standards, invention and production from industrial development.

restore-past-order.rationale: Described the Republican party as ever a party of progress and urged a way forward rather than a return to the past.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred: held that production depends on rewarding effort and ruled out an economy based on altruism alone.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred: treated the profit motive as the stimulus to production and held that production and its fair division go together.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Named the dictatorship of the proletariat among catchwords that clothe hatred and destruction and called the Russian system a tyranny.

taxation-theft.rationale: Raised taxes in 1932 and described taxes as the means to settle sharing of the surplus.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Held that intelligence, character and the divine spark belong to individuals rather than groups and that the state must not make man its pawn.

positive-liberty.rationale: Said liberation from widespread poverty gave a higher degree of individual freedom and made equality of opportunity the core of American individualism.

total-state.rationale: Condemned regimentation and the idea of the servitude of the individual to the state.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said the US has no desire for territorial expansion or domination of other peoples and that its ideals negate imperialism.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Called balancing the federal budget the first necessity of national stability and the foundation of recovery, and urged expenditure cuts and new taxes against deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Said liberalism rests on the realization that economic freedom cannot be sacrificed if political freedom is to be preserved.

national-self-determination.rationale: Reproduced Wilson's self-determination principle and criticized the peace settlement for failing to deliver it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Wrote that society needs spiritual forces and that faith inspires individualism, while also distrusting the emotion of the crowd.

class-collaboration.rationale: Brokered cooperation of employers and labor leaders against wage cuts and strikes and rejected class strata and class conflict as foundations.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described government as the umpire of the social system maintaining equality before the law, not a tool of one class.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Backed public education, health services, regulation, public works and relief loans beyond defense and justice.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said government secures equality before the law, equality of franchise and equal opportunity, while rejecting equality of ability.

separated-powers.rationale: Said self-government requires decentralization and many checks and balances to safeguard liberty.

party-controls-media.rationale: Argued that expanded government business leads to control of press and platform and that free speech does not outlive free industry.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred: rejected political engagements like League membership that commit the US in advance.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred: held that political freedom cannot last without economic freedom and condemned Soviet tyranny as an economic failure.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Described property as a useful and necessary instrument that stimulates initiative and selects leadership, rather than an object in itself.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Described the Russian regime as socialism applied nationally and as having failed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Said the world had been disillusioned by the divine right of kings and denied that divinity rests in any ruling class or person.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Abhorred autocracy and held that officials may not choose which laws to enforce.

ban-cartels.rationale: Said laws must maintain competition and destroy conspiracies against smaller units, and urged rigid enforcement of competition law.

no-bailouts.rationale: Founded the Reconstruction Finance Corporation to lend to banks, insurers and railways and defended its support of the credit structure.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Praised the founders for not granting hereditary titles and landed estates and said children must not inherit power by right of birth.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Held that the system evolves within itself and that depressions are transitory from which the nation emerges stronger.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Described a broader sense of service and responsibility to others as part of individualism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: In The Challenge to Liberty grouped Nazism, fascism, socialism, communism and regimentation as sharing the servitude of the individual to the state.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Wrote that rising standards of living, including non-essentials, need no apology and are the base of civilization.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Said the system crumbles if citizens choose which laws to support; dislike of a law gives a duty to discourage violation and a right to work for repeal.

non-intervention.rationale: Issued the Clark Memorandum, ended the Nicaragua occupation and pledged non-interference in Latin America, but threatened intervention in the Dominican Republic and sent warships to El Salvador.

defeat-communism.rationale: Condemned the Bolsheviks yet opposed intervention in 1919; later opposed alliance with Stalin and called the USSR morally repugnant.

religion-illusion.rationale: Said individualism rests on the divine spark in every human being and on spiritual forces.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Praised the economic individualism that drove invention, production and living standards, though he rejected the label capitalism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Said American individualism is not capitalism, socialism or a cross of them, while praising its economic results; mixed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Defended free speech, free press and assembly as the core of liberalism and warned bureaucracy erodes them.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Sought arms reduction and arms conferences while keeping the army and navy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: said the sons of the successful should not hold their fathers' places of power by right of birth.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Argued that property assembled in groups controlling the state makes capital an oppressor and that economic domination by a few must not be tolerated.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Reviewer: personal spiritual faith is nearby evidence, not a stated view on state promotion of atheism in schools; no recorded position found.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Called rigid and expeditious justice the first safeguard of freedom and pushed to strengthen federal law enforcement and prisons.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Held that relief should come through voluntary community and local-government action, and opposed any direct or indirect federal dole.

person-over-state.rationale: Wrote that individualism rests on the worth of each person and in 1934 attacked the idea of the servitude of the individual to the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Wrote that people do not live by bread alone and that spiritual forces must inspire the social and economic system.

arms-reduction.rationale: Signed the London Naval Treaty, called for further decreases in naval and other arms and a general disarmament conference.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Held that the divine spark is in every human being and that individualism admits it in all.

farm-price-support.rationale: Denounced proposals for government buying, selling and price-fixing of farm goods as state socialism, though he created the Federal Farm Board to stabilize markets.

simple-living.rationale: Praised rising material standards and the spread of comforts as the base of civilization.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Held that citizens who dislike a law must seek repeal and not violate it.

notes: Born 10 August 1874 in West Branch, Iowa; died 20 October 1964 (checked against Wikipedia). The Challenge to Liberty (1934) and Freedom Betrayed could not be downloaded in full, so the New Deal views rest on a scholarly account of the former and on Wikipedia for his foreign policy after 1939. Mexican repatriation, the Bonus Army and civil-rights questions are left null: his personal direction of repatriation is disputed, and no answer to a specific statement rests on them. His views on Prohibition (enforcement, no repeal) are not covered by a statement.
